clue.text: Stable without a runner

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the stable word goes around the A

parts.note: a manger is the feeding trough found in a stable, standing for it here

explanation.surface: A horse stable is left with no horse fit to race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' reads as a racehorse, but it is the definition: someone who runs a business. 'Without' means outside, putting MANGER around A.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who runs an organisation or team is its manager, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Carriage sounds cheap

indicators.note: the word for stingy, spoken, gives the answer's sound

parts.note: mean means stingy or cheap

explanation.surface: A horse-drawn coach makes a shabby, cheap noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carriage' is how a person carries themselves, not a coach.
explanation.definitionFit: Mien is a person's bearing or demeanour, how they hold themselves.

clue.text: Send up article if too unsophisticated

indicators.note: in a down clue, sending a word up reverses it

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper article mocks something for being too simplistic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Send up' works in a down clue because the word is written upwards; 'too' is only a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Naif, a variant of naive, describes someone innocent and lacking worldliness.

clue.text: For this, proverbially, we have no information

definitions.text: For this, proverbially, we have no information

parts.words: For this, proverbially, we have no information
parts.note: the proverb says that having no news is itself welcome

explanation.surface: A remark about lacking any information.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb 'no news is good news' equates absence of information with welcome tidings.

clue.text: Provoke audible discord

indicators.note: audible means heard, so the word for quarrels is spoken

parts.note: rows are quarrels, a form of discord

explanation.surface: To stir up quarrelling that can be heard.
explanation.walkthrough: ROWS here rhymes with cows (quarrels).
explanation.definitionFit: To rouse someone is to stir them up or provoke them into action.

clue.text: The Spanish weapons involved in the movement of arms

definitions.text: involved in the movement of arms

parts.note: el is the Spanish masculine definite article
bows are weapons that fire arrows

explanation.surface: Spanish weaponry plays a part when armed forces are on the move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movement of arms' suggests troops shifting weapons; it means bending your arms, which happens at the joints.
explanation.definitionFit: The joints in the middle of each arm do the bending whenever the arms move.

clue.text: Any clue is pointless and wrong for such folly

indicators.note: wrong signals the letters are put in the wrong order
E is a compass point, so a pointless word loses that letter

explanation.surface: A crossword clue without point and incorrect is madness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pointless' drops E (east, a compass point) from CLUE; 'wrong' rearranges ANY plus CLU. 'Is' and 'for such' link.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunacy means madness or extreme foolishness, so it serves for folly.

clue.text: Speaker swallows one drink as a starter

indicators.note: swallows means takes in, so the speaker contains the others

parts.note: an orator is a public speaker
one is the Roman numeral I
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: A public speaker downs a single drink as an aperitif.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' reads as a first course or appetiser; it means one who starts something.
explanation.definitionFit: An originator is the person who starts or creates something.

clue.text: That half-warmed fish, for example

parts.note: the phrase is a swapped-sound version of 'that half-formed wish', attributed to a famous Oxford don

explanation.surface: A lukewarm piece of fish offered as a sample.
explanation.walkthrough: William Spooner, warden of New College Oxford, was said to swap the opening sounds of words.
explanation.definitionFit: Swapping initial sounds, as in 'half-formed wish', is the classic slip named after Spooner.

clue.text: Close of play

parts.note: read as the end of a theatrical play rather than the end of a day's cricket

explanation.surface: Stumps are drawn at the end of the day's game.
explanation.definitionFit: The closing speech or section after a drama's main action is its concluding passage.

clue.text: Looking blue, I'd go in for treatment

indicators.note: something treated is processed and changed, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone feeling low decides to check into hospital for treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For treatment' rearranges I'D GO IN; 'Looking' just links to the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo is a deep shade of blue between blue and violet in the spectrum.

clue.text: Place of secret laughter

parts.note: from the idiom about laughing up a garment's arm when amused privately

explanation.surface: A hidden spot where people go to giggle.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom is 'laughing up your sleeve', meaning amused in secret.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom of laughing up one's arm covering makes it where secret amusement happens.

clue.text: Having thought about it, no!

parts.note: the word no seen in a mirror reads as on, so the answer's phrase describes how to make the clue's word

explanation.surface: Someone reconsiders and firmly changes their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation 'no!' is the result: the reflection of ON in a mirror gives NO.
explanation.definitionFit: After consideration is the idiomatic meaning of the adverbial phrase, synonymous with thinking it over.

clue.text: Performance in which the middle section gets the twitch

definitions.text: Performance in which the middle section gets the twitch

parts.words: Performance in which the middle section gets the twitch
parts.note: the middle section is the torso's midriff, made to ripple in a dance

explanation.surface: A show where the central part of the orchestra gets nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle section' reads as part of an orchestra or show; it is the stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: A Middle Eastern dance centres on rippling the abdominal muscles.

clue.text: Classification of chocolates?

parts.note: a sorting into kinds, also the word for a mixed box of sweets

explanation.surface: A question about sorting a box of chocolates.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a sorting into groups and also a mixed selection, like a box of chocolates.

clue.text: Batsman's delight or bowler's pushover?

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a pitch that plays true and is easy to score runs on
a batsman's dismissal that comes very cheaply for the bowling side

explanation.surface: A cricket pitch that pleases one side and gifts the other an easy dismissal.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the wicket is both the pitch itself and a batsman's dismissal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket uses the phrase both for a benign batting surface and for a dismissal gained cheaply.

clue.text: Is unable to get a girl into bed

indicators.note: into means the girl goes inside the bed word

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A man fails to persuade a woman to sleep with him.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a seduction failing; 'to get a' only links, and 'Is unable' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannot is the negative of can, meaning is not able.

clue.text: Dry bearing?

definitions.meaning: to dry out washing by exposing it to the atmosphere

explanation.surface: A question about whether a dry part is a mechanical bearing.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means expose to dry out; as a noun it means manner or demeanour.

clue.text: Balls — those that go on till morning?

definitions.meaning: in cricket, short-pitched deliveries that bounce high and are easy to hit

definitions.text: those that go on till morning?
definitions.meaning: dances lasting a long time, hops being informal dances

explanation.surface: Dances that keep going until dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: A long hop in cricket is a poor, short ball; a 'hop' is also an informal dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket's name for loose short deliveries, and literally protracted dances.

clue.text: Sign the French love

parts.note: le is the French masculine definite article
love is zero in tennis scoring, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: A French romantic writes their name with affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love' is nil in tennis, so it gives O.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo, the lion, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Unseemly do on cruise trip

indicators.note: a trip is a stumble, so these letters fall over into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Bad behaviour at a party held on board a cruise ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trip' looks like part of the holiday, but it signals that DO ON CRUISE is rearranged; 'do' is not a party here, just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecorous behaviour offends against good taste, so it is improper or unseemly.

clue.text: Tea licence for Swiss Cottage

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea
a let is a permission or allowance, as in letting a property

explanation.surface: Tea and a permit at a London district named Swiss Cottage.
explanation.walkthrough: Swiss Cottage is a district of London, but here it is a cottage in Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalet is a wooden cottage of the type found in the Swiss Alps.

clue.text: Bottle of booze?

parts.note: bottle in its slang sense of nerve, which some find by drinking

explanation.surface: A simple question about a container of alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle' is British slang for courage, so the clue asks for nerve that comes from drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the false bravery gained from drinking alcohol.

clue.text: Nautical hazards means one shortens sail

definitions.meaning: ridges of rock or coral just below the sea's surface
to roll in part of a sail to reduce its area in strong wind

explanation.surface: A sailor explains how to cope with dangers at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Means' links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names underwater rock ridges; the verb means to take in part of a sail.

clue.text: Kind of line used by a puffer

definitions.meaning: as in a pipeline carrying oil or gas
the bowl-and-stem device a tobacco smoker puffs on

explanation.surface: A fishing line used by a pufferfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puffer' suggests a fish or train; it is a smoker.
explanation.definitionFit: It prefixes a kind of supply line and names a smoker's tobacco device.

clue.text: Word associated with poker — it's not flush

definitions.meaning: a card game variant with some cards dealt face up
a ... stands proud of a surface rather than level with it

explanation.surface: A card player notes that a hand isn't a flush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flush' reads as a poker hand; it means level with a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: It names a poker variant, and a projecting knob that is not level.

clue.text: Sewer used for the introduction of drugs

definitions.meaning: one who sews, a tool for stitching, not a drain

definitions.text: used for the introduction of drugs
definitions.meaning: the sharp hollow point of a syringe that delivers an injection

explanation.surface: A drain used to smuggle narcotics into a place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sewer' reads as a drain; it is something that sews.
explanation.definitionFit: The same slim pointed instrument stitches cloth and, on a syringe, injects medicine.

clue.text: Fellow entertained by robbery — he enjoys the fun

indicators.note: to be entertained by is to be taken in as a guest, so the fellow goes inside

parts.note: a heist is a robbery
a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: A man who finds a robbery entertaining is just having fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fellow' reads as a man in general, but in crosswords a fellow is often a university don; 'he enjoys the fun' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A hedonist is a pleasure-seeker, someone who lives for enjoyment.

clue.text: What is left in the car

definitions.meaning: the property and money a person leaves at death
a car with a long body and a rear door for luggage

explanation.surface: Asking what has been left behind in the vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: An estate car is the British name for a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: It means a dead person's assets and also a type of station-wagon car.

clue.text: Force one to hang about instead of going to work

definitions.text: Force one to hang about instead of going to work

parts.words: Force one to hang about instead of going to work
parts.note: the verb that means to hang something up also means to bar an employee from work for a time

explanation.surface: Someone is made to loiter rather than head off to the job.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both hanging something up and barring a worker from duty temporarily.
